01 / Civic technology

When someone needs blood, the search should start closer to home.

City Sheba starts with blood donor discovery in Hajiganj. Its shared API gives the mobile and web apps a common set of rules for donor profiles.

Explore City Sheba ↗

02 / Workflow tools

A task can change. The original instruction should stay within reach.

Fieldnotes separates the editable task from its source. Try drafting a checklist and see what happens when you rewrite a task without losing its context.

Explore Fieldnotes ↗

03 / Local commerce

A delivery network begins at the handoff.

For Hajiganj, the first question is whether kitchens, riders, and customers can coordinate a few reliable routes. That is the premise of the local commerce pilot concept.

Explore Local Commerce ↗

04 / Applied AI

Before AI writes the pitch, someone should be able to check the research.

The AI Sales Employee concept puts prospect evidence beside the outreach draft, so a reviewer can check the details before a message leaves their desk.

Explore AI Sales Employee ↗

03 / WHAT WE BUILD

Three ways we put software to work.

01WEB PRODUCTSMake complex work easier to follow.

Dashboards, task tools, and shared workspaces that show people what changed and what they can do next.

See the Fieldnotes prototype ↗
02MOBILE APPSDesign for the moment someone needs it.

A resident looking for a blood donor has a different task from someone browsing a directory at home. Mobile flows should reflect that urgency.

See the City Sheba project ↗
03APPLIED AIKeep the evidence next to the output.

When software drafts a message or suggests an action, the person reviewing it needs a clear way to check the source and edit the result.

See the AI Sales Employee concept ↗

04 / WHERE WE STARTED

Hajiganj gave us our first questions.

How do you find a blood donor when time matters? How does a neighborhood kitchen reach customers a few streets away? Obayed and Yasin started OOYI in Bangladesh to build products around questions they could investigate firsthand.

Meet the founders ↗

05 / HOW WE BUILD

From first question to first pilot.

We narrow an idea into something people can try, then use their feedback to decide what to build next.

01 /

Discover

Observe the workflow and identify where people lose time or context.

02 /

Prototype

Build one usable flow around the hardest part of the problem.

03 /

Pilot

Test with the people who would use it and document what changes.

04 /

Improve

Use those findings to decide what to fix and what to build next.
